diagnosis_summary: Rock's public issue discussion and 16.6 source distinguish the unsubscribe link placed in a message footer from the email-client one-click control presented near message headers. The footer is a browser GET to Rock's preference experience, while one-click is carried in List-Unsubscribe headers and handled as a POST. Rock 16.3 release notes separately record one-click support, Email Preference Entry behavior for one-click requests, and the fix tracked by issue 5770. Issue 6040 itself was closed as clarification, not as a confirmed defect or fixed-version claim.
workaround_summaries: When validating one-click unsubscribe, inspect the delivered message's List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers and the receiving email client's native control separately from the footer link. Do not make a browser GET auto-unsubscribe, because automated link scanners can issue GET requests.

verification_playbook.goal: Distinguish Rock's footer preference link from standards-based one-click unsubscribe on an already delivered message.
prerequisites: Use an existing non-sensitive test message delivered by the Rock communication path being assessed.
Do not click an unsubscribe control while inspecting it.

steps.title: Inspect one-click headers
steps.instructions: View the raw headers of the existing test message and record only whether List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post are present. Do not retain addresses, tokens, message IDs, or header values.
steps.expected_if_affected: The expected headers are absent even though the communication configuration and release should provide one-click support.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: Both headers are present; the receiving client may still choose whether to display its native control.

steps.title: Compare native and footer surfaces
steps.instructions: Observe, without clicking, whether the email client displays a native unsubscribe control and whether the message footer contains Rock's preference link. Treat them as separate mechanisms.
steps.expected_if_affected: Headers expected for one-click are missing; absence of a client-native control alone is inconclusive.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: Headers are present and the footer remains a separate browser preference link, regardless of the client's display choice.
evidence_to_record: native control displayed yes or no
footer preference link displayed yes or no

limitations: Email-client UI is not authoritative because providers apply their own reputation and display policies.
Do not test by issuing the one-click POST against a real recipient subscription from production.
